text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Swiss philosopher HENRI DUNANT, who founded the Swiss Red Cross, was born in 1828.
Australian cartoonist CLAUDE MARQUET, whose classic "The Blood Vote" became an anti-conscription poster, was born in 1869.
American President HARRY S. TRUMAN, who ordered the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, was born on this day in 1884.

South African/British comedian SID JAMES was born in 1914. His 'comfortable' face made him a favourite on tv shows like "Hancock" and "Bless This House". His film-making career took a back seat during the making of the movie "Stromboli" when news of his romance with actress INGRID BERGMAN erupted in scandal around the world.
British naturalist and documentary film-maker SIR DAVID ATTENBOROUGH was born in 1926.
American heavyweight boxing champion SONNY LISTON was born in 1932.
American novelist PETER BENCHLEY, best known for "Jaws", was born in 1940.

British singer and songwriter GARY GLITTER (PAUL GADD) was born in 1940. His musicial career began in the late fifties, after a series of line-up changes and name changes he began appearing as GARY GLITTER in 1972. His hits included "Rock & Roll" (1972), "I'm The Leader Of The Gang" (1973), "I Love You Love Me Love" (1973), "Always Yours" (1974) and "Another Rock & Roll Christmas" (1984). In 1988 the British band 'Timelords' immortalised him in their song "Doctorin' The Tardis" with the line "Everybody loves GARY GLITTER".

American singer and actor RICK NELSON was born in 1940 as ERIC HILLIARD. He had his brother DAVID became early teen idols in the fifties, after appearing on their parents radio and television shows. Hits included "A Teenager's Romance" (1957), "Poor Little Fool" (1958), "Hello Mary Lou" (1961), "Teenage Idol" (1962), "It's Up To You" (1962) and "For You" (1963).

American singer TONI TENNILLE (The Captain and Tennille) was born in 1943. She was successful with her husband DARYL DRAGON with million sellers such as "Love Will Keep Us Together" (1975), "The Way I Wanna Touch You" (1975), "Shop Around" (1976)
and "Do That To Me One More Time" (1979).
Former leader of the Australian Democrats, JANINE HAINES, (who retired from politics and is now making good money on the 'speaking circuit') was born in 1945.
American actress CANDICE BERGEN ("Murphy Brown") was born in 1946.
US drummer with 'Talking Heads' and 'Tom Tom Club' CHRIS FRANTZ was born in 1951.
US drummer and songwriter ALEX VAN HALEN was born in 1955. He and brother EDWARD formed 'Mammoth', 'Rat Salade' and then 'Van Halen' in 1974. They started to chart regularly after 1978.
** EVENTS **
1429 : France's warrior maiden, JOAN OF ARC, led the
DAUPHIN's troops to victory over the English laying seige to Orleans.
1846 : The Battle of Palo Alto was won by General
ZACHARY TAYLOR and his American troops against Mexican forces.
1854 : British walker Captain BARCLAY ALLARDICE, died. He
was an accomplished long-distance walker, at one time covering 1,000 miles in 1,000 consecutive hours!
1876 : The last full-blood Aborigine from Tasmania,
TRUGANINI, died. TRUGANINI was the daughter of Bruny Island tribal chief MANGANA, and kept to traditional Aboriginal culture, despite efforts to 'Europeanise" Tasmanian Aborigines.
1889 : Dame NELLIE MELBA made her debut in Paris, playing
OPHELIA in "Hamlet".
1901 : The Federal Labor Party was founded in Australia.
1902 : Mont Pelee on Martinique erupted and destroyed the
town of St Pierre; over 30,000 people died.
1921 : Sweden abolished the death penalty.
1924 : Afrikaans became the official language of South
Africa.
1945 : Street parties were held all over Britain,
celebrating V.E DAY, marking the end of World War Two.
1955 : Hiroshima victims arrived in the United States for
plastic surgery.
1961 : Former British diplomat GEORGE BLAKE was jailed
for 42 years for spying for the Soviet Union.
1987 : Democratic front-runner GARY HART withdrew from
the United States' Presidency race, following allegations of an affair with model DONNA RICE.
1990 : The Baltic State of Estonia adopted its 1938
constitution, affirming its independence from the Soviet Union.
1991 : A British Government report was issued,

identifying dozens of Nazi war criminals living in Britain. The report followed an investigation shortly after the end of World War Two, but its findings were kept secret by the intelligence organisation MI5.
